response:
[
  "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended first‑line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness and for melanoma in situ.",
  "Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness.",
  "Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor and in the same operative setting whenever possible.",
  "When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1–3 mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.",
  "Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia.",
  "The 7‑point score is driven by the presence of a blue‑whitish veil and localized irregular pigmentation.",
  "The blue‑whitish veil criterion is present and contributes 2 points to the score.",
  "The localized irregular pigmentation criterion is present and contributes 1 point to the score.",
  "The blue‑whitish veil is a confluent blue pigment with overlying white haze.",
  "Localized irregular pigmentation refers to asymmetric blotches.",
  "These two visual features are major and minor criteria, respectively, and together support the elevated score.",
  "The clinician should verify the presence of a blue‑whitish veil and localized irregular pigmentation on the image."
]
